stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Amazon pilots ad services in ChatGPT
stories.author: thm
bullet_points: Amazon is testing the integration of advertising services within ChatGPT.
This signals a major shift toward monetizing large language models (LLMs) through advertising.
The move indicates a significant industry trend toward commercializing generative AI platforms.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation and utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.
The focus is on tracking and benchmarking a specific, powerful LLM variant from Meta.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with popular local LLM runners.

stories.title: Mathematicians want proof OpenAI didn’t use their work
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: A second mathematician is challenging OpenAI regarding the data used to train its mathematical models.
The accusations center on unethical behavior, dishonesty, and a lack of transparency regarding the origins of the AI's discoveries.
This follows a previous dispute concerning whether OpenAI benefited from unpublished academic work.

stories.title: Six Chinese AI firms accused of aggressively copying US frontier models
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Six Chinese AI firms are accused of aggressively copying US frontier AI models.
The US government is reportedly urging AI companies to identify and secretly downgrade Chinese users to less capable models.
The story highlights escalating geopolitical tensions surrounding AI technology and intellectual property.

stories.title: Apple's long-rumored foldable becomes reality with the $2,000 iPhone Duo
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Apple is launching its first foldable device.
The device is reportedly named the iPhone Duo.
It is expected to be available next month with a starting price of $2,000.

stories.title: Apple starts preorders for Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 with new Health Sensing System
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Apple has initiated preorders for the upcoming Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 models.
The new wearables will feature an advanced Health Sensing System.
The devices are expected to integrate new features powered by Apple Intelligence.

stories.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
stories.author: Mike Zheng Shou
bullet_points: Introduces Show-Harness, an Embodied Harness designed to bridge the gap between high-level VLM intelligence and low-level robot control.
The system allows Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to 'play' robots by reasoning over discrete semantic action units.
It uses embodiment-specific interpreters to deterministically translate abstract semantic intents into concrete, local robot actions.

stories.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
stories.author: John Sous
bullet_points: Introduces SemiGroup-JEPA (SG-JEPA) to enhance Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models.
Addresses a key limitation of current JEPA models: the untested capability to learn and generate physically realistic dynamics.
Achieves this by supplying physics parameters to the temporal model via action-conditioning and joint training.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: ConvMem proposes a new method to handle extremely long contexts in LLMs, addressing the limitations of fixed context windows.
It aims to overcome the high latency and costly Reinforcement Learning (RL) training associated with existing sequential context extension methods like MemAgent.
The research focuses on integrating convolutional memory mechanisms to improve long-context reasoning capabilities.

stories.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
stories.author: Agoritsa Polyzou
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLM memorization of sensitive or undesirable training data.
Proposes 'Layer-Selective Unlearning' as an efficient alternative to costly full model retraining.
Aims to create more robust LLMs by ensuring forgotten knowledge remains stable even after deployment optimizations like quantization.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the context length limitation of Large Language Models (LLMs) for long-context reasoning.
Proposes 'ConvMem,' a convolutional memory approach to overcome the latency and RL training costs of sequential memory methods (like MemAgent).
Focuses on improving LLM scalability and efficiency when processing extremely large amounts of text data.

stories.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
stories.author: Yi Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of geometric reasoning in AI, a known weakness in current models.
Proposes a framework to enhance pure LLMs, allowing them to rival state-of-the-art LMMs in complex geometry.
The solution integrates a 'Geometric Vision Parser' to translate visual diagrams into a format usable by the LLM.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Sure, Meta’s AI Muse works, but it sure creeps me out
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta has released its new AI assistant, Muse, as part of its push into AI-powered productivity tools.
Muse is designed to automate 'busywork' across various tasks, including shopping, email management, and trip planning.
The article presents a critical user review of the tool, highlighting both its functionality and user apprehension regarding its nature.

stories.title: How the iPhone Duo compares to other folding phones
stories.author: Brad Bourque
bullet_points: Apple is launching a foldable phone, dubbed the iPhone Duo, on October 23rd.
The device is priced at $1,999, positioning it competitively against high-end Android foldables like the Galaxy Z Fold 8.
The iPhone Duo enters the established market segment dominated by Android manufacturers like Samsung and Google.

stories.title: Four groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Multiple hacking groups were found utilizing an identical exploit kit targeting Chrome and Windows.
The incident highlights the ongoing risk posed by unpatched software vulnerabilities.
The article suggests AI-driven vulnerability discovery is accelerating the pace of security threats.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to accurately measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route and capabilities, rather than just model identifiers.
Addresses the industry problem where current benchmarks only score advertised model IDs, ignoring crucial deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a gold-blind preflight check and a reliability-inclusive scoring rule to ensure measurable, deployable AI capabilities.

stories.title: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
stories.author: Haifeng Wang
bullet_points: JarvisGUI addresses a gap in current AI agent research by focusing on cross-device GUI interactions.
The research tackles the complexity of real-world workflows requiring state maintenance and coordination across heterogeneous platforms.
It critiques existing benchmarks for being too narrow, focusing only on single-device, statically defined tasks.

stories.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
stories.author: Eray Tüzün
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of unbounded memory growth and retrieval degradation in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Introduces 'Fortunate Recall' (FR), a policy layer that manages memory lifecycle based on fact type.
Classifies personal facts into a behavioral ontology (10+1 categories) to apply differential persistence policies.

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: The paper investigates the feasibility of using Foundation Models (specifically VLMs) for consistent online content moderation.
It compares two methods for guiding these models: an instruction-driven approach (reasoning from policy precepts) versus an example-driven approach.
The research addresses the critical challenge of operationalizing increasingly complex content moderation policies.

stories.title: Cross-Model Agreement as a Deployment-Time Reliability Signal for Automatic Polyp Segmentation
stories.author: Jitin Singla
bullet_points: Addresses a critical problem in real-time medical AI (colonoscopy) where ground truth is unavailable during inference.
Introduces Referee-Based Quality Estimation (RBQE), a reference-free framework to assess model reliability.
Evaluated on a standardized external benchmark, suggesting practical applicability in clinical deployment.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to accurately measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route and capabilities, rather than just model identifiers.
Addresses the industry problem where current benchmarks only score advertised model identifiers, ignoring critical deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a 'gold-blind capability-binding preflight' to verify execution contracts before task evaluation.

stories.title: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Electrical Faults and Power Quality Disturbances in Aerospace Power Systems
stories.author: Berker Peköz
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in power quality monitoring by applying deep learning to high-frequency (400 Hz) aerospace power systems, unlike traditional 50/60 Hz grid methods.
Introduces a hardware-aware deep learning framework specifically designed for multiclass detection of electrical faults and power quality disturbances.
Uses a high-fidelity simulation model inspired by real-world aerospace architecture (e.g., Boeing 787) for validation.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route, rather than just model identifiers.
Highlights a critical issue where current benchmarks only score advertised model IDs, ignoring crucial deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a scoring rule that accounts for reliability.

stories.title: Building Multilingual Bridges: Data Mixing as the Pillar of Generalization for In-Language Reasoning
stories.author: Julia Kreutzer
bullet_points: Current reasoning language models exhibit strong English-centric bias, limiting accessibility for non-English speakers.
The research proposes 'Data Mixing' as a core method to improve multilingual generalization in reasoning models.
The goal is to advance L2 reasoning, enabling models to reason consistently in the language of the prompt.

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: The paper investigates the feasibility of using Foundation Models (specifically VLMs) for consistent online content moderation.
It compares two methods for guiding model behavior: instruction-driven (reasoning from policy precepts) versus example-driven approaches.
The research addresses the critical industry challenge of operationalizing complex content moderation policies reliably.

stories.title: Retrofitting Code Using LLMs to Support Exceptional Behavior
stories.author: Milos Gligoric
bullet_points: The paper addresses the manual tedium of adding Exception Related Code (ERC) to large software codebases.
It proposes a novel task: retrofitting existing, ERC-less code using Large Language Models (LLMs).
The process is guided by providing the LLM with the original code and associated Exceptional Behavior Tests (EBTs).

stories.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
stories.author: Mounîm A. El Yacoubi
bullet_points: Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) are advancing rapidly in video understanding tasks like captioning and QA.
The primary bottleneck for VideoLLMs is their high computational and memory cost, which scales with video length.
The paper surveys various inference-efficiency mechanisms aimed at making these models deployable in real-time and resource-constrained environments.

stories.title: Rust Is Tier-1 Language at Microsoft
stories.author: mmastrac
bullet_points: Microsoft has officially recognized Rust as a Tier-1 language.
This indicates a significant endorsement of Rust's capabilities within a major tech corporation.
The news suggests increasing industry adoption and maturity of Rust in enterprise environments.

stories.title: Rust Is Tier-1 Language at Microsoft
stories.author: rustfoundation.org via mmastrac
bullet_points: Rust has achieved Tier-1 language status within Microsoft.
This indicates a significant internal adoption and investment in the Rust programming language at Microsoft.
The news signals a growing industry trend towards using memory-safe languages like Rust in large-scale enterprise environments.

stories.title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
stories.author: sylwia-lask
bullet_points: The article posits that AI is rapidly surpassing human developers in coding proficiency.
It argues that coding itself is not the most critical skill in software development.
The piece suggests a shift in the value proposition of human developers in the age of advanced AI.

stories.title: The Verification Bottleneck in AI-Generated Software
stories.author: kenwalger
bullet_points: AI code generation speed is increasing rapidly.
A critical issue remains regarding the correctness of AI-generated software.
The article addresses the 'verification bottleneck' in AI-assisted development.
